summary: A form from David Crocker asking sites to supply information about their ARPANET TIPs, the Terminal IMPs used to reach the network. The collected details were meant to give TIP users more flexibility and make network use easier. Responses were to be sent to him, preferably as a NIC Journal entry.

eli5.summary: A paper form asking people who set up the network's dial-in boxes to describe them, so users can learn how to use them.

subtitle: A form to collect information about terminal access points on the ARPANET.

tldr.problem: TIP users on the early ARPANET needed more information about how to access and use each terminal access point, but that information was scattered and incomplete.
tldr.mechanism: David Crocker at UCLA created a standard form to ask each site to document their TIP setup, staffing, features and local contact information.
tldr.outcome: The collected responses would let users find the right TIP for their needs and contact local operators for help.

today: RFC 352 is a historical document recording an early effort to organize network infrastructure information. It reflects the practical challenges of coordinating a growing distributed system in the early 1970s.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: In the early 1970s, the ARPANET was growing and users needed ways to access it from remote locations. TIPs (Terminal Interface Message Processors) were hardware devices that let dial-up users connect to the network. RFC 352 is a request for information: a form David Crocker designed to let TIP sites tell the network community about their setup and services.
sections.eli5: TIPs were boxes you could call up to join the network. This is a form asking the people running them to describe what they have.

sections.title: The Information Form
sections.content:
The form asks TIP sites to provide: the organization name and pseudo-host number; the regular host computer used by the organization; a mailing address; and the name and contact details of the local person responsible for TIP operations and the TIP operator, if any.

It also requests information about TIP options and special features such as magnetic tape, printers and card readers; scheduled downtime; and port-level details including terminal types or dial-up phone numbers.
sections.eli5: The form asks who runs the TIP, where they are, who can help, what features it has, when it shuts down, and what phone numbers or terminals connect to it.

sections.title: Making the Network Easier to Use
sections.content: The RFC explains the goal plainly: to provide additional information for TIP users so they can gain more flexibility in how they use the network. Crocker asked sites to send responses back to him, preferably as a NIC Journal entry to make the information easier to organize and store.
sections.eli5: When sites fill out the form and send it back, all users can then look up how to reach any TIP and find the right one for what they need.
